theme: Every human being is losing as time passes, except those with four qualities: faith, righteous deeds, urging one another to the truth, and urging one another to patience.
story: Usually counted as a very early Makkan surah, though some place it in Madinah. Its few words are built to stick in the memory after one hearing.
Whenever two Companions met, they would not part until one had recited this surah to the other. It was said that if people reflected on it, it alone would be enough for them.

Before accepting Islam, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ reportedly recited it to Musaylimah, who claimed to be a prophet. Musaylimah answered with nonsense of his own, and ʿAmr told him: “You know that I know you are lying.”

sections.title: By time, mankind loses except with faith, good deeds, truth and patience
sections.meaning: Allah swears by time that every human being is in loss. The only ones saved are those who believe, do righteous deeds, urge one another to the truth, and urge one another to patience.
points: Except those who believe and do righteous deeds
And urge each other to truth and to patience
sections.matters: In three short ayat it lays out the way to success and the way to ruin. The first two qualities perfect yourself; the last two help perfect others. Being good alone is not enough.
sections.story: No specific incident. Its weight shows in how the Companions recited it to each other whenever they met.
explained: Al-ʿaṣr is time, the days and nights in which people act, good or bad; it can also mean late afternoon or the ʿAṣr prayer. Life is capital that melts like an ice-seller’s stock: every passing breath takes a piece. So al-insān, every human, is in khusr, loss.

Only four qualities stop the loss: īmān, faith; ʿamal ṣāliḥ, righteous deeds; tawāṣī bil-ḥaqq, urging each other to the truth; and tawāṣī biṣ-ṣabr, urging each other to patience, in obeying Allah, in keeping away from sin, and in bearing painful decrees.
teaches: Time is your capital; every moment spent is gone.
Doing nothing is also a loss.
Faith must show in righteous deeds.
Don’t only be good yourself; call others to the truth.
Patience is needed to obey, to avoid sin and to bear hardship.
sections.hook: Three ayat, opening page 601. Ayah 3 lists four qualities in two pairs, and the second pair repeats tawāṣaw: bil-ḥaqq, then biṣ-ṣabr.

groups.text: Allah swears by time that every human being is in loss.
Except those who believe, do good, and urge one another to the truth and to patience.

1.explain: Wal-ʿaṣr: by time, the days and nights in which every deed is done. Other meanings: the late afternoon, or the ʿAṣr prayer.

2.explain: Khusr: loss, the opposite of profit. Every human loses the capital of his life as it passes, fully or in part, unless he spends it well.

3.explain: Four qualities end the loss: faith, righteous deeds, urging one another to ḥaqq (faith and good deeds, or the Quran) and to ṣabr, patience in obeying Allah, avoiding sin and bearing trials.
